hero.text: Simple 40-minute lessons in three stages, each built on a unit activity in the government Pupil's Book.

blocks.heading: What a PPP lesson is
text: PPP stands for **Presentation, Practice and Production**. The teacher first presents a small piece of language in a clear situation. Pupils then practise it in controlled tasks, and finally use it for a purpose of their own. It suits large classes because each stage has a clear start and end, and it fits the activity sequence of the Sri Lankan Pupil's Books well.
Each plan below gives the book unit and activity, the learning outcome, the materials, and what happens in each stage with timings for a 40-minute period. Adapt the timings to your own timetable.

blocks.title: About these plans
text: Grade 3 is taught mainly through listening and speaking. Keep writing short and let pupils say everything before they write it. Stage times are for a 40-minute period; shorten them if your period is 30 minutes.

Every plan on this page was written by RCF English. The unit and activity names refer to the government Pupil's Book so that you can find the right page; no textbook text is reproduced here. Download it as an editable Word document or a print-ready PDF.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, I, myself and me
facts: Say your name; Make your badge
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to greet a friend and say their own name using Hello! I'm ... and What's your name?
Paper badges, crayons, a soft ball

stages.name: Presentation
text: Wave and say Hello! I'm Teacher. Repeat with two pupils. Hold up a name badge and model: What's your name? My name is ...

stages.name: Practice
text: Class repeats the two lines, then halves of the class say them to each other. Pass the ball: the pupil holding it answers What's your name? and asks the next pupil.

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils make and colour a name badge, then walk around and greet five friends using the badge.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Sing a hello song together.

printBlocks.homework: Say Hello! I'm ... to three people at home.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 1: Greeting and saying your name. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 1, I, myself and me
facts: Count, read and say; How old are you?
Numbers one to ten and saying your age
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to count from one to ten and say how old they are.
Number cards 1 to 10, the picture page with the children's ages

stages.name: Presentation
text: Count ten pencils aloud, holding up a number card for each. Model: How old are you? I'm eight.

stages.name: Practice
text: Pupils count in pairs, taking turns (Work in pairs. Take turns). Show a number card; pupils say the number and the word.

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils read the speech bubbles (Hi, I'm Kumar. I'm eight years old.) and then say the same about themselves to a partner.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Count back from ten to one together.

printBlocks.homework: Count ten things at home and draw them.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 1: Numbers one to ten and saying your age. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 1, I, myself and me
facts: Listen and say; Play the game
Saying your grade and where you live
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to say which grade they are in and where they live.
A ball, a simple map of the area

stages.name: Presentation
text: Model: I'm in grade three. I live in Matara (use your own town). Ask two pupils What grade are you in? Where do you live?

stages.name: Practice
text: Chorus and pair repetition of the two questions and answers.

stages.name: Production
text: Play the ball game from the book: pupils in a circle pass the ball asking Where do you live? and answering I live in ...

stages.name: Check and close
text: Three pupils introduce themselves with name, age, grade and town.

printBlocks.homework: Draw your house and write I live in ... under it.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 1: Saying your grade and where you live. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 2, Home sweet home
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name family members and introduce them with This is my ...
Family picture from the book, word cards (mother, father, brother, sister)

stages.name: Presentation
text: Point to the family picture: This is my father. This is my mother. Stick the word cards next to each person.

stages.name: Practice
text: Pupils point and say as the teacher names each member. Teach the Family Tree song line by line.

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils draw their own family and introduce it to a partner: This is my sister. She is a girl.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Sing the song again with actions.

printBlocks.homework: Bring a family photo or drawing.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 2: Family members. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 3, Our School
facts: Places and people in the school
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name places in the school and match people with their jobs.
Picture cards: library, office room, music room, playground, herbal garden; job cards

stages.name: Presentation
text: Walk the class to the door and point: This is the playground. That is the library. Show the job cards: Principal, Teacher, Librarian, Security guard.

stages.name: Practice
text: Read aloud the place names from the book. Listen and match: the teacher describes a person and pupils point to the right card.

stages.name: Production
text: Pairs play I'm thinking of a place: one pupil mimes (reading, dancing) and the other names the place.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Pupils name their favourite place in the school.

printBlocks.homework: Draw one place in the school and write its name.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 3: Places and people in the school. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 4, My food bag
facts: Talk; Look and find; Listen and make a food bag
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name common fruits and vegetables and say which ones they like.
Real fruits and vegetables or pictures, a paper bag

stages.name: Presentation
text: Take fruits out of a bag one by one: This is a banana. This is a carrot. Model: I like mangoes.

stages.name: Practice
text: Look and find: pupils point to each fruit in the book picture. Sort the picture cards into fruits and vegetables.

stages.name: Production
text: Listen and make a food bag: the teacher says four items and pupils draw them in a paper bag shape, then tell a partner what is in their bag.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Class says which fruit most pupils like.

printBlocks.homework: Draw your favourite fruit and write I like ...
printBlocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 4: Fruits and vegetables. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 5, Animal friends
facts: Look and say; Listen to the poem and recite
Animals and their sounds and actions
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name animals, copy their actions and recite a short poem.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show animal pictures and name them. Make each animal's sound and action. Model: It is a cat. It says miaow.

stages.name: Practice
text: Look and say, then Look and find in the book picture. Listen to the poem and recite it line by line.

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils make a simple mask (Make a mask) and act out the animal while the class guesses.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Recite the poem with actions.

printBlocks.homework: Tell your family the name of three animals in English.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 5: Animals and their sounds and actions. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 6, Clothes we wear
facts: Sing this song; Look, read and match
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name clothes with their colours using has / I have.
Real clothes (a hat, a belt, a scarf), colour cards

stages.name: Presentation
text: Put on a hat: I have a blue hat. Point to a pupil: Nimal has a white shirt.

stages.name: Practice
text: Sing the song (Sonia has a blue hat...) and point to the clothes. Look, read and match the clothes words with the pictures.

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils describe what they are wearing to a partner: I have a white shirt and a blue short.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Two pupils describe a friend while the class guesses who.

printBlocks.homework: Draw your favourite clothes and colour them.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 6: Clothes and colours. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 6, Clothes we wear
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to read and say o'clock, quarter past, half past and quarter to.
A cardboard clock with moving hands

stages.name: Presentation
text: Move the clock hands: It is seven o'clock. It is half past seven. Show quarter past and quarter to.

stages.name: Practice
text: Pupils read the times in the book. The teacher sets the clock; pupils say the time.

stages.name: Production
text: Pairs draw a clock face, set a time and ask What's the time?

stages.name: Check and close
text: Ask: What time do you come to school?

printBlocks.homework: Draw a clock showing the time you wake up.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 6: Telling the time. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 7, Playing is fun
facts: Listen, repeat and act; Let's play a game
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to follow and give simple action instructions such as run, jump and kick.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Do the actions while saying them: Run! Jump! Kick the ball! Show Look! The ball rolls fast.

stages.name: Practice
text: Listen, repeat and act: pupils copy the teacher. Simon says with the action words.

stages.name: Production
text: Small groups play a game while one leader gives the instructions in English.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Pupils name the game they liked best.

printBlocks.homework: Teach one action game to a brother or sister.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 7: Action words for games. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 11: Unit 8, The world around me
facts: Listen, point and repeat; Listen and read
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name things in a garden and describe a tree using It has ...
A picture of a garden, a real leaf and a small branch

stages.name: Presentation
text: Point to the garden picture: This is a tree. It has leaves. It has branches. Show the real leaf and branch.

stages.name: Practice
text: Listen, point and repeat the garden words: bush, path, tree, pond, swing, fence. Read This is my garden. It has big trees.

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils draw their own garden or school garden and tell a partner three things it has.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Say the Mother Nature lines together: Save water. Plant a tree.

printBlocks.homework: Water a plant at home and tell the class tomorrow.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 3, Unit 8: Things in a home garden. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

Grade 4 is still taught mainly through listening and speaking, with short reading and writing. Let pupils say everything before they write it. Stage times are for a 40-minute period.

Every plan on this page was written by RCF English. The unit and activity names refer to the government Pupil's Book so that you can find the right page; no textbook text is reproduced here. Download it as an editable Word document or a print-ready PDF.

blocks.title: Complete lesson plan books are coming
text: These are simple sample plans. **Complete lesson plan books for every grade** will be part of **RCF Premium Resources**, which will be ready in the future. [See RCF Premium Resources](premium-resources/)

printBlocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, My family and friends
facts: Greeting people and saying where you live
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to greet a friend, answer How are you? and say their name and where they live.
The Hello! song, name cards, a simple map or picture of the town

stages.name: Presentation
text: Greet pupils one by one: Hello, how are you? Answer for them: I'm fine, thank you. Teach the song from Lesson 1, then the answers I'm great / fine / good / okay.

stages.name: Practice
text: Pupils practise the exchange in pairs (Practise with your friend). Model Lesson 2: I'm Sandani. I live in Matara. Pupils repeat with their own names.

stages.name: Production
text: Mingle: pupils greet five friends and ask What's your name? Where do you live?, then tell the class about one friend.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Three pupils introduce a friend: This is Nisal. He lives in Galle.

printBlocks.homework: Write four sentences about yourself: name, age, grade, town.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 1: Greeting people and saying where you live. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 1, My family and friends
facts: Talking about my family and parts of the body
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to say how many people are in their family and name parts of the body.
A family drawing on the board, body-part word cards

stages.name: Presentation
text: Draw your own family and say: There are four people in my family. This is my mother. Point to parts of the body and name them: head, neck, eyes, shoulder.

stages.name: Practice
text: Groups of three introduce their families (Lesson 4). Listen and repeat the body-part words, then Simon says with them.

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils draw their family, label one person, and tell a partner: There are ... in my family. My brother has curly hair.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Two pupils show their drawings to the class.

printBlocks.homework: Label a drawing of yourself with six body-part words.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 1: Talking about my family and parts of the body. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 2, Our beautiful garden
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to describe a garden using There is one ... and There are three ...
The Unit 2 garden picture, real leaves or flowers

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show the garden picture: There is a tree. There are three birds. Write the rule: there is + one thing, there are + many things.

stages.name: Practice
text: Listen, point and say the garden words: trees, birds, butterflies. Talk about Senuri's garden with the sentence frame (Lesson 1).

stages.name: Production
text: Spot-the-difference in pairs (Lesson 5): each pupil says five sentences with there is / there are.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Correct: There is three birds → There are three birds.

printBlocks.homework: Draw your home garden and write five sentences about it.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 2: There is and there are. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 2, Our beautiful garden
facts: Garden work: verbs, tools and following instructions
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name garden tools, say what people do in a garden, and follow a set of instructions.
Pictures of a rake, ekel broom and watering can; paper and crayons

stages.name: Presentation
text: Mime watering and sweeping: I water the plants. She waters the plants. Show the tool pictures and name them (Lesson 3).

stages.name: Practice
text: Listen and repeat the action words: pick, water, sweep, plant. Match tools with the actions they are used for.

stages.name: Production
text: Listen and do (Lesson 6): pupils follow six instructions to draw and colour a garden picture, then check with a partner.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Compare pictures: who followed every instruction?

printBlocks.homework: Write four things you can do in a garden.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 2: Garden work: verbs, tools and following instructions. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 3, Places around me
facts: Places in my village or town
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name places in their area and say what people do there.
Picture cards: temple, church, post office, library, school, market

stages.name: Presentation
text: Hold up each card: This is a post office. We buy stamps here. Drill the place names with the class.

stages.name: Practice
text: Look and say (Lessons 1 and 2) with the pictures in the book. Quick game: the teacher says what people do; pupils name the place.

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils draw a simple map of their village with four places and tell a partner about it.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Two pupils name the places nearest their homes.

printBlocks.homework: Draw and label four places near your home.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 3: Places in my village or town. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 3, Places around me
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to give and follow directions using go straight, turn right and turn left.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Walk across the classroom saying: Go straight. Turn left. Stop. Show the arrow cards with the words.

stages.name: Practice
text: Listen and trace the route on the map (Lesson 3).

stages.name: Production
text: Pairs give directions from the school gate to a place on their own map; the partner traces it.

stages.name: Check and close
text: One pair demonstrates for the class.

printBlocks.homework: Write three directions from your home to school.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 3: Giving simple directions. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 4, Joy of work
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name common occupations and say where each person works.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show the cards: This is a doctor. A doctor works in a hospital. Build two columns on the board: person and place.

stages.name: Practice
text: Listen, point and say the occupations (Lesson 1) and the workplaces (Lesson 2). Match each worker with a workplace.

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils tell the class about one worker they know: My uncle is a farmer. He works on a farm.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Ask: what do you want to be?

printBlocks.homework: Draw a worker and write two sentences about the job.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 4: Occupations and workplaces. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 5, Our festivals
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name the festivals they celebrate, say which month each falls in, and name festive food.
Festival pictures, a calendar, food pictures

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show the pictures: This is the Vesak festival. It is in May. Write the pattern: ... is in ... (month).

stages.name: Practice
text: Look and read (Lessons 1 and 2), then match festivals with months. Name the festive food: milk rice, watalappan (Lesson 5).

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils tell a partner about their favourite festival: what they wear, eat and do.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Two pupils tell the class.

printBlocks.homework: Draw your favourite festival and write four sentences.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 5: Festivals, months and festive food. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 5, Our festivals
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to ask and answer What are you doing? using is / are + verb + ing.
Action picture cards from the unit

stages.name: Presentation
text: Mime cooking and ask: What am I doing? Answer: You are cooking. Write the pattern is / am / are + verb + ing.

stages.name: Practice
text: Act out the Lesson 4 dialogue in pairs. Match and speak (Lesson 7) using the pictures.

stages.name: Production
text: Mime chain: one pupil mimes a festival activity, the class asks What are you doing?, the pupil answers.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Check spelling: making, cooking, singing.

printBlocks.homework: Write four sentences about what your family does at a festival.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 5: What are you doing? (present continuous). A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 6, Let's go shopping
facts: This, these, that, those and shopping talk
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use this / these and that / those and take part in a short shopping conversation.
Classroom objects, price cards, a shop corner

stages.name: Presentation
text: Hold up one pen: This is a pen. Point far: That is a bag. Repeat with plurals. Model the shop talk: Can I help you? I want two mangoes.

stages.name: Practice
text: Look and match (Lesson 2). Read the Lesson 3 dialogue in pairs.

stages.name: Production
text: Set up a class shop: pupils take turns as seller and buyer, using this / these / that / those and asking the price.

stages.name: Check and close
text: One pair performs their shopping scene.

printBlocks.homework: Write a five-line shopping conversation.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 6: This, these, that, those and shopping talk. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 11: Unit 7, My calendar
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to say the days of the week, the months of the year and today's date.
A class calendar, day and month cards

stages.name: Presentation
text: Sing the days-of-the-week song (Lesson 1). Say the months in order, then show dates: Second - 2nd, third - 3rd.

stages.name: Practice
text: Listen and repeat the days and months (Lessons 2 and 3). Read the dates aloud (Lesson 4) and find them on the class calendar.

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils make their own balloon calendar (Lesson 5) with the months and their birthday marked, then tell a friend: My birthday is on the 5th of June.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Ask three pupils today's date.

printBlocks.homework: Write the date of your birthday and two family birthdays.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 7: Days, months and dates. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 12: Unit 7, My calendar
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to describe the weather and tell the time on the hour and half hour.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show the weather cards: It is sunny. It is rainy. Move the clock hands: It is eight o'clock. It is half past eight.

stages.name: Practice
text: Listen and repeat the weather words (Lesson 6), then sing the weather song. Practise telling the time (Lesson 7).

stages.name: Production
text: Pairs ask and answer: What's the weather like today? What time do you get up?

stages.name: Check and close
text: Set the clock and ask three pupils the time.

printBlocks.homework: Draw clocks for four things you do every day.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 7: Weather and telling the time. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 13: Unit 8, Playing games
facts: Action words and saying what you like
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name action words, say what someone is doing now, and say which game they like.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Mime and say: walk, run, hop, skip (Lesson 1). Show the pattern: He is running. I like cricket.

stages.name: Practice
text: Listen and mime the action words. Listen and repeat the is / am / are + verb + ing sentences (Lesson 3).

stages.name: Production
text: Talk to five friends (Lesson 6): pupils ask What game do you like? and report: Amali likes netball.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Count which game the class likes best.

printBlocks.homework: Write four sentences about the games you like.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 8: Action words and saying what you like. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 14: Unit 9, Good practices
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use Excuse me, May I ...? and thank you, and say what good practices they follow.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Model politeness: Excuse me, may I come in? Thank you. Read two good practices from Lesson 3: Let's keep it clean.

stages.name: Practice
text: Act out the Lesson 2 dialogue in pairs. Read and match the good practices with the pictures (Lesson 3).

stages.name: Production
text: Groups take a situation card (in the bus, in the library, at the canteen) and act out the polite way to behave.

stages.name: Check and close
text: The class names the polite words they heard.

printBlocks.homework: Write four good practices for your class.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 9: Polite words and good practices. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 15: Unit 10, Happy days
facts: Feelings and acting out a story
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to say how they feel and act out a short dialogue with expression.
Feeling cards: hungry, thirsty, tired, happy, sad

stages.name: Presentation
text: Mime being hungry and thirsty: I am hungry. I want to eat. Show the feeling cards and drill them.

stages.name: Practice
text: Listen and match the feelings with the pictures (Lesson 1). Read the Lesson 4 dialogue aloud with the class.

stages.name: Production
text: Groups read and act out the dialogue (Lesson 4), showing the feelings in their voices and faces.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Two groups perform; the class names the feelings shown.

printBlocks.homework: Draw a happy day and write four sentences about it.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 4, Unit 10: Feelings and acting out a story. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

text: These are simple sample plans. **Complete lesson plan books for every grade** will be part of **RCF Premium Resources**, which will be ready in the future. [See RCF Premium Resources](premium-resources/)

printBlocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, Hello
facts: Introductions with am, is and are
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to introduce themselves and a classmate and choose am, is or are correctly.
The Unit 1 role play, a chart of am / is / are

stages.name: Presentation
text: Introduce yourself: I am Mrs Perera. I am your English teacher. Point to pupils: This is Nimal. He is in Grade 6. They are friends. Build the chart: I – am; he / she / it – is; we / you / they – are.

stages.name: Practice
text: Read the role play in pairs. Chain drill: each pupil says I am ... and introduces the next pupil. Do Activity 7 (am, is or are) and check with a partner.

stages.name: Production
text: Groups of three write and act a short first-day meeting, using am, is and are at least five times.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Two groups perform; the class listens for am, is and are.

printBlocks.homework: Write five sentences about your family using am, is and are.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 1: Introductions with am, is and are. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 2, Leisure Lesson
facts: What people are doing now (present continuous)
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to describe actions happening now with is / are + -ing.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Mime writing and ask What am I doing? Write You are writing. Show the pattern am / is / are + verb-ing and spelling changes (swim – swimming, make – making).

stages.name: Practice
text: Mime-and-guess with verb cards: She is swimming. Complete Activity 5.

stages.name: Production
text: Pairs describe the Unit 2 picture aloud, then write four sentences (Activity 6).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Check three -ing spellings on the board.

printBlocks.homework: Write what five family members are doing at 7 p.m. tonight.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 2: What people are doing now (present continuous). A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 3, Where's Everything?
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to say and write where things are with in, on, under, near, next to and between.
A box, a pen, classroom objects

stages.name: Presentation
text: Use the box and pen: The pen is in / on / under the box. Place a book between two bags and write each preposition with a sketch.

stages.name: Practice
text: Pair work: list classroom objects and say where they are (Activity 3). Write sentences about the picture (Activity 4).

stages.name: Production
text: Listen and draw (Activity 6), then pupils describe their own picture for a partner to draw.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Compare drawings: which pairs matched?

printBlocks.homework: Write five sentences about your bedroom.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 3: Prepositions of place. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 4, What Can You See?
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use this / these for near things and that / those for things far away.
Objects placed near and far from the teacher

stages.name: Presentation
text: Hold a pen: This is a pen. Point to one far away: That is a pen. Repeat with plurals. Draw a near / far, one / many table.

stages.name: Practice
text: Complete Activity 1. Point-and-say game.

stages.name: Production
text: Activity 2: six sentences about things in and outside the classroom, using all four words.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Read three sentences; the class points near or far.

printBlocks.homework: Label a drawing of your table with four sentences.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 4: This, that, these, those. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 5, Aunt Minoli's Kitchen
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to give instructions for a simple recipe using imperatives and first, next, then, finally.
Step pictures for making tea, sequence word cards

stages.name: Presentation
text: Act out making tea: First, boil the water. Next, put tea leaves in the pot. Point out that each instruction starts with a verb.

stages.name: Practice
text: Match the soup steps with the pictures (Activity 1). Order the tea steps and add sequence words (Activity 2).

stages.name: Production
text: Groups write steps for a simple snack; one pupil reads while another mimes.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Did the mime follow the order?

printBlocks.homework: Write six steps for something you make at home.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 5: Instructions in order. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 6, What We Do
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to ask and answer about routines and report them with the -s form.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Tell your routine: I get up at 5 o'clock. Change it: She gets up at 5 o'clock. Underline the -s.

stages.name: Practice
text: Drill Do you ...? Yes, I do. / No, I don't. Find someone who (Activity 4).

stages.name: Production
text: Report to the class (Activity 5) and write the findings (Activity 6).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Correct He get up → He gets up.

printBlocks.homework: Write about a family member's day in six sentences.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 6: Daily routines (present simple). A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 7, A Fine Day
facts: Weather words and on / in / at
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to name the weather and use on for days, in for months and at for times.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show the calendar: My birthday is in June, on the 12th, at 4 o'clock. Build the rule table.

stages.name: Practice
text: Listen and name the weather symbols (Activity 3). Complete the on / in / at sentences.

stages.name: Production
text: Pairs interview each other about birthdays and times and write three true sentences.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Quick-fire: time word → preposition.

printBlocks.homework: Keep a weather diary for three days.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 7: Weather words and on / in / at. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 8, A Visit to the Zoo
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to say what people and animals can and cannot do.

stages.name: Presentation
text: A fish can swim. A fish can't climb. Show that can never takes -s.

stages.name: Practice
text: Match sentences and pictures (Activity 5). Complete the chart in pairs (Activity 6).

stages.name: Production
text: Tell the class about yourself and a friend (Activity 7): I can swim, but my friend can't.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Vote on the most surprising ability.

printBlocks.homework: Write six sentences about what you can and can't do.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 8: Ability with can and can't. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 9, Sugar or Sand
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to replace repeated nouns with the correct pronoun.
A short repetitive text on the board, the Unit 9 story

stages.name: Presentation
text: Read: Amal has a bag. Amal's bag is red. Ask what sounds strange. Rewrite with pronouns and list them.

stages.name: Practice
text: Circle the pronouns (Activity 5). Match and replace (Activities 6 and 7).

stages.name: Production
text: Pairs rewrite a paragraph that repeats a name, using pronouns.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Two pairs read aloud.

printBlocks.homework: Write about a friend using five pronouns.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 9: Pronouns. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 10, Was It Yesterday?
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to say what they did yesterday with regular and irregular past forms.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Tell a story: Yesterday I visited my grandmother. I went by bus. Sort the verbs into +ed and irregular.

stages.name: Practice
text: Find the past forms in the role play (Activity 2). Complete the diary flow chart (Activity 4).

stages.name: Production
text: Each pupil says one thing they did yesterday (Activity 5) and writes three more.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Add new verbs to the class table.

printBlocks.homework: Write a six-sentence diary entry about last weekend.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 10: The simple past. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 11: Unit 11, Eco Friends
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to write a short paragraph about their free time with reasons.
The Unit 11 role play, a paragraph frame

stages.name: Presentation
text: Read the role play and list what the friends like to do. Model: In my free time, I like to read because ...

stages.name: Practice
text: Build a word bank. Pairs talk about what they like and why.

stages.name: Production
text: Write a five- or six-sentence paragraph (Activity 2) using like to / enjoy and because.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Swap: one thing done well, one to improve.

printBlocks.homework: Add a picture and bring it to display.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 6, Unit 11: Free-time activities. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

blocks.title: Complete lesson plan books are coming
text: These are simple sample plans. **Complete lesson plan books for every grade** will be part of **RCF Premium Resources**, which will be ready in the future. [See RCF Premium Resources](premium-resources/)

printBlocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, What You See
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to give the opposite of common adjectives and pick out words with similar meanings.
Picture pairs (big / small, hot / cold), word cards

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show picture pairs and elicit the opposites. Explain synonyms with warm – hot and happy – glad.

stages.name: Practice
text: Write opposites under the pictures (Activity 3) and match opposites (Activity 4). Circle the two synonyms in each set (Activity 5).

stages.name: Production
text: Pairs describe a classmate's bag with three adjectives; the partner replies with the opposites or a synonym.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Opposites race: teams of two, teacher calls a word.

printBlocks.homework: Write ten opposite pairs of your own.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 1: Opposites and synonyms. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 2, Friends Indeed
facts: Reading a story and writing instructions
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to answer questions on Fifi's story and write clear instructions in order.
Fifi's story, instruction strips cut up for ordering

stages.name: Presentation
text: Pre-teach glass, spacious and freely, then read Fifi's story aloud. Show how instructions begin with a verb and use then, next.

stages.name: Practice
text: Answer the Activity 1 questions in pairs. Put the cut-up instructions in order (Activity 2).

stages.name: Production
text: Groups design a simple anti-dengue poster and write four instructions to go with it (Activity 3).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Groups show their posters.

printBlocks.homework: Write five instructions for looking after a pet.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 2: Reading a story and writing instructions. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 3, Pleasure
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use was / were for the past and will be for the future when telling a story.
The Perahera dialogue, the Merryland story

stages.name: Presentation
text: Act out the Perahera dialogue with two pupils. Draw a timeline: yesterday – was / were, tomorrow – will be.

stages.name: Practice
text: Fill in the Merryland story with was, were or will be (Activity 5). Listen and match letters to the playground passage (Activity 7).

stages.name: Production
text: Pairs tell each other about a festival they saw and one they will see.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Three pupils report their partner's answers.

printBlocks.homework: Write six sentences about a festival, past and future.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 3: Was, were and will be. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 4, A Busy Day
facts: Reading a notice and possessive pronouns
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to find information in a notice and use mine, yours, his, hers, ours and theirs.
The scout notice, pupils' own pens and books

stages.name: Presentation
text: Act out Lahiru's busy day. Pick up a pupil's pen: Is this yours? Yes, it's mine. Build the list.

stages.name: Practice
text: Complete the table from the notice (Activity 3). Fill in the possessive pronouns (Activity 9).

stages.name: Production
text: Lost-property game: the teacher collects objects and pupils claim them using the pronouns.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Correct: This book is her's → hers.

printBlocks.homework: Write a notice for a class event.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 4: Reading a notice and possessive pronouns. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 5, Once Upon a Time
facts: Joining sentences with and, but, or and when
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to combine short sentences using and, but, or and when.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show two strips: Early people lived in caves. They hunted animals. Join them with and. Contrast and, but, or and when with examples.

stages.name: Practice
text: Combine the sentences (Activity 3). Join sentences with when (Activity 8).

stages.name: Production
text: Groups speak about the journey of human civilisation, each pupil giving one joined sentence (Activity 4).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Note the best joined sentences on the board.

printBlocks.homework: Write a short paragraph about a museum visit using when twice.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 5: Joining sentences with and, but, or and when. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 6, Better Safe Than Sorry
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to give advice and rules with must and should and write a short note.
The Suganya dialogue, a get-well card

stages.name: Presentation
text: Act out Suganya is Absent Today. Write rules and advice: You must wash your hands. You should rest.

stages.name: Practice
text: Complete the sentences with must, should, would or can (Activity 3).

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils write Suganya's thank-you note to her friends (Activity 4).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Read two notes aloud.

printBlocks.homework: Make a get-well card for someone you know.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 6: Must, should, would and can. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 7, Around the Country
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use adverbs to describe how things happen and speak for one minute about a place.
Ruvini's speech, A Trip to Jaffna, adverb cards

stages.name: Presentation
text: Read Ruvini's speech. Pupils answer the Activity 1 questions. Show adverbs: The train went slowly. They arrived safely.

stages.name: Practice
text: Fill in the adverbs (Activity 6).

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils choose a place and speak about it for a minute (Activity 8).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Class gives one compliment to each speaker.

printBlocks.homework: Write a description of a place you visited.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 7: Adverbs and speaking about places. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 8, Wonders Around Us
facts: Reading for information and daily schedules
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to take notes in a table from descriptions and talk about their daily schedule.
Pictures of famous monuments, a blank table

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show the monuments and ask what pupils know. Model a schedule: 6.30 a.m. – I have breakfast.

stages.name: Practice
text: Match descriptions and pictures (Activity 2) and complete the table (Activity 3).

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils write their own schedule and compare it with a partner (Activity 6).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Pairs report one difference.

printBlocks.homework: Find one fact about a Sri Lankan monument.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 8: Reading for information and daily schedules. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 9, Our Beautiful World
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use up, down, over, into, below and next to to describe a picture.
The Unit 9 picture, a toy car or ball

stages.name: Presentation
text: Move a toy: It goes up the hill. It goes over the bridge. Write the prepositions with arrows.

stages.name: Practice
text: Complete the sentences about the pictures (Activity 4).

stages.name: Production
text: Describe the picture with the given words (Activity 5), then do the describe-and-draw task (Activity 6).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Compare drawings with the originals.

printBlocks.homework: Write five sentences about your way to school.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 9: Prepositions of movement. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 10, Future
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to make and discuss predictions about life in the future.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Read two predictions and ask Will this come true? Show will / won't + verb.

stages.name: Practice
text: Make sentences with will / won't (Activity 7). Discuss the predictions (Activity 2).

stages.name: Production
text: Groups write and present a prediction for one category (Activity 3).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Class votes on the most likely prediction.

printBlocks.homework: Write five predictions about your village in 2050.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 7, Unit 10: Predictions with will and won't. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

text: These are simple sample plans. **Complete lesson plan books for every grade** will be part of **RCF Premium Resources**, which will be ready in the future. [See RCF Premium Resources](premium-resources/)

printBlocks.heading: Plan 1: Unit 1, Plan the Work, Work the Plan
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use myself, yourself, himself and so on correctly in sentences.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Act out 1.1. Pick out We did it ourselves. List the reflexive pronouns beside the subject pronouns.

stages.name: Practice
text: Answer the 1.2 questions. Rearrange the words into sentences (1.3).

stages.name: Production
text: Pairs describe something they did by themselves last week.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Correct hisself → himself.

printBlocks.homework: Write five sentences about things you do yourself.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 1: Reflexive pronouns. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 2: Unit 1, Plan the Work, Work the Plan
facts: Plural nouns and a friendly letter
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to form regular and irregular plurals and plan a friendly letter.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Write a cup, a boot, a knife, a child and elicit the plurals. Read Amitha's letter aloud; label its parts.

stages.name: Practice
text: Write the plurals (1.7).

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils write a short letter to a pen friend about a trip they are planning.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Check the address and greeting layout.

printBlocks.homework: Finish the letter neatly.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 1: Plural nouns and a friendly letter. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 3: Unit 2, Winged Friends
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to express rules, needs and advice with must, have to / has to and should.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Contrast: You must wear a seat belt (rule). You should rest (advice). Add have to / has to.

stages.name: Practice
text: Build sentences from the table (2.5). Complete the blanks (2.6).

stages.name: Production
text: Write three sentences each with the three forms and their negatives (2.7).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Pairs read and correct each other.

printBlocks.homework: Write rules for looking after birds.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 2: Must, have to and should. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 4: Unit 3, Let's Be Considerate
facts: Joining sentences with since and as
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to join a reason and a result using since and as.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Act out 3.1. Show: Since it was raining, we stayed home.

stages.name: Practice
text: Join the sentences (3.3).

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils write three sentences about kind acts using since and as.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Share the kindest act.

printBlocks.homework: Write a short paragraph on courtesy.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 3: Joining sentences with since and as. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 5: Unit 3, Let's Be Considerate
facts: Reading a story aloud and tongue twisters
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to read aloud clearly with good pace and pronunciation.
The Magic Words story, tongue twisters

stages.name: Presentation
text: Model-read part of The Magic Words. Say the tongue twisters slowly, then faster.

stages.name: Practice
text: Pairs read the story, taking turns by paragraph.

stages.name: Production
text: Groups perform the story as a short drama with the magic words.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Tongue twister challenge.

printBlocks.homework: Practise one tongue twister at home.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 3: Reading a story aloud and tongue twisters. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 6: Unit 4, Mother Nature
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use prepositions in instructions and label a picture from a description.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Review prepositions with classroom objects. Read the 4.6 instructions aloud.

stages.name: Practice
text: Put the instructions in the correct order (4.6).

stages.name: Production
text: Listen and label the picture (4.7), then pairs describe their own picture.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Check labels together.

printBlocks.homework: Write instructions for planting a tree.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 4: Prepositions and instructions. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 7: Unit 5, Between the Miles
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to add -ly, -ful, -ness and -less to base words and use comparatives and superlatives.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show care → careful, careless, carefully. Compare three pupils' heights: taller, the tallest.

stages.name: Practice
text: Complete the table (5.2) and the worksheet (5.6).

stages.name: Production
text: Pupils describe one of the smallest things they know (5.5).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Share one comparison.

printBlocks.homework: Write six comparison sentences about your family.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 5: Word building and comparisons. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 8: Unit 6, When We Are Together
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to recognise and form present simple passive sentences.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show English is spoken all over the world. Ask who speaks it. Build be + past participle.

stages.name: Practice
text: Match the roti pictures with the steps (6.5). Fill in the verb forms (6.6).

stages.name: Production
text: Find the passive sentences in A Day in the Life of a News Reader (6.7) and describe how tea is made in the passive.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Read two passive sentences aloud.

printBlocks.homework: Describe how a local food is made.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 6: The passive voice (present). A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 9: Unit 7, The World of Children
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to rewrite past events in the passive and write a descriptive letter.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show: Sigiriya was built by King Kashyapa. Review letter layout.

stages.name: Practice
text: Rewrite the historical events in the passive (7.3).

stages.name: Production
text: Order the Sigiriya information (7.8) and write Sahan's letter (7.9).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Peer-check the layout.

printBlocks.homework: Write about a place you visited.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 7: Past passive and a letter. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 10: Unit 8, It's a Small World
facts: Future passive and writing an article
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use will be + past participle and write a short news article.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show: The match will be played tomorrow. Point out the parts of a newspaper article.

stages.name: Practice
text: Complete the sentences (8.4 and 8.5).

stages.name: Production
text: Write a short article in steps (8.7) about a school event.

stages.name: Check and close
text: Read two headlines aloud.

printBlocks.homework: Collect one English news headline.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 8: Future passive and writing an article. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 11: Unit 9, On Top of the World
facts: By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely and never.

stages.name: Presentation
text: Place the adverbs on the scale. I always brush my teeth. I never ...

stages.name: Practice
text: Fill in the conversation (9.2) and write sentences from the pictures (9.3).

stages.name: Production
text: Group sentence chain (9.4), then write a paragraph (9.5).

stages.name: Check and close
text: Check adverb position.

printBlocks.homework: Write about your weekend habits.
printBlocks.caption: Grade 8, Unit 9: Adverbs of frequency. A 40-minute PPP lesson.

printBlocks.heading: Plan 12: Unit 10, Beyond the Classroom
facts: The past perfect and telling stories
By the end of the lesson, pupils will be able to use the past perfect to show which past action happened first.
The English Day conversation, a timeline

stages.name: Presentation
text: Show: When I arrived, the bus had left. Draw two past points on a timeline.

blocks.title: About these plans
text: Grades 12 and 13 share one General English textbook with eight units, so there is no separate Grade 12 or Grade 13 book. These twenty plans (ten for each year) follow the eight units in order. Your school's scheme decides which units fall in Grade 12 and which in Grade 13. Stage times are for a 40-minute period.

Every plan on this page was written by RCF English. The unit and activity names refer to the government Pupil's Book so that you can find the right page; no textbook text is reproduced here. Download it as an editable Word document or a print-ready PDF.

blocks.title: Where these come from
text: The competencies and competency levels below are taken from the **NIE English Language Teachers' Guides** for each grade. Each grade keeps its own guide's numbering and wording, because the guides do not always number the same level in the same way. Always check against the Teachers' Guide your school is using.

**Not included yet:** the primary grades, Grades 12 and 13 (A/L General English) and English Literature, because we do not have those Teachers' Guides. The **new 2026 Grade 6 syllabus** uses a different set of competencies; the Grade 6 table here follows the earlier syllabus.

blocks.heading: The eight competencies (Grades 6 to 11)
rows: Identifies the sounds of English Language
Uses mechanics of writing with understanding
Engages in active listening and responds appropriately
Builds up vocabulary using words appropriately and accurately to convey precise meaning
Extracts necessary information from various types of texts
Uses English grammar for the purpose of accurate and effective communication
Uses English creatively and innovatively in written communication

blocks.heading: Grade 6 competency levels
intro: **Source:** Grade 6 Teachers' Guide (edition implemented from 2015). 47 competency levels.
This is the Grade 6 syllabus that the 2014 to 2019 Pupil's Book follows. The new 2026 Grade 6 syllabus uses a different set of competencies; schools following it should use the new Teachers' Guide.
rows: Reads aloud different types of texts accurately and meaningfully
Uses capital and simple letters appropriately
Listens and follows instructions and responds to requests

blocks.title: These are samples, not official instructions
text: Each tool is set out in the usual **School Based Assessment tool** format. Fill in your school's name and the date. **For Grades 6 to 11 English, the competency and competency level numbers are taken from the NIE English Language Teachers' Guides** for those grades (see [Competency Levels by Grade](teacher-resources/competency-levels/)). The Grade 6 guide used is the edition implemented from 2015, so schools on the new 2026 Grade 6 syllabus should use the numbers in the new guide. For primary grades, A/L General English and Literature we do not yet have the Teachers' Guides, so the competency wording there is a sample: copy the official competency and level from your guide. Follow the SBA plan and circulars for your grade and year for the number of tools, their timing and how marks are recorded. The terms shown in the Literature tools are suggestions; change them to suit your school's plan.

blocks.heading: SBA plan 1: Show and tell
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
1 to 2 minutes per pupil (over two periods)
Uses simple spoken English to talk about familiar things.
Names and describes a familiar object in simple sentences. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
Things at home and in school; colours and sizes
Pupils will be able to say three simple sentences about an object they bring from home.
Models a short show-and-tell with an object, gives the sentence frames (This is my ... It is ... I like it because ...), and calls pupils one by one.
Bring an object from home and say at least three sentences about it to the class.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Names the object in a full sentence
Speaks clearly enough to be understood
Speaks with confidence and little prompting

blocks.heading: SBA plan 2: Listen and do
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Listens to and follows simple spoken instructions.
Responds correctly to one-step and two-step instructions. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
Pupils will be able to carry out simple instructions given in English.
Gives instructions one at a time (Stand up. Touch your nose. Colour the ball red.), repeating each once, and records each pupil's responses on a checklist.
Listen and carry out each instruction, including drawing and colouring on a worksheet.

blocks.heading: SBA plan 3: My picture book
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Writes simple sentences about familiar topics.
Writes one or two sentences to match a picture. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
Pupils will be able to write simple, correctly punctuated sentences about their own pictures.
Shows a sample picture book, revises capital letters and full stops, and helps pupils plan four pages.
Draw four pictures about their family or school and write one or two sentences under each.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Every picture has a matching sentence
Capital letters and full stops are correct

blocks.heading: SBA plan 4: Reading aloud
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Reads short texts aloud with understanding.
Reads a practised text accurately and fluently. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
A short practised passage of about 60 words
Pupils will be able to read a short passage aloud accurately, in phrases, with a clear voice.
Chooses and practises the passage with the class, then listens to each pupil and marks on a class sheet.
Read the practised passage aloud to the teacher.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Reads in phrases, not word by word
Pauses at full stops and commas

blocks.heading: SBA plan 5: Role play
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
One period for preparation, 3 minutes per pair
Competency 8: Communicates clearly, fluently and concisely
8.13 Uses language in variety of contexts (Grades 6 and 7)
Asking for and giving directions / shopping
Students will be able to complete an everyday conversation using the expressions from the unit.
Revises the useful expressions, gives each pair a situation card, and assesses each pair during the performance.
Prepare and act out the situation in pairs, with a clear start and end.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Completes the task in the situation
Speaks fluently with few long pauses
Pronounces clearly and responds to the partner

blocks.heading: SBA plan 6: Instruction poster
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Competency 7: Uses English creatively and innovatively in written communication
Preventing dengue / making a cup of tea
Students will be able to write at least six clear instructions using imperatives and sequence words.
Shows a model poster, revises imperatives and sequence words, and gives the topics.
Make a poster with a heading, pictures and at least six instructions in order.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Relevant instructions in the right order
Clear layout with heading and pictures
Neat and readable from a distance

blocks.heading: SBA plan 7: Reading log
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Competency 5: Extracts necessary information from various types of texts

5.5 Reads and understands simple folk stories (Grade 7) / Reads and responds to simple folk stories / stories (Grade 8) / Reads and responds to simple folk tales (Grade 9); 5.6 Extracts the general idea of a text (Grades 7, 8 and 9)
Three short books or stories chosen by the student
Students will be able to summarise stories and give reasons for their opinions.
Explains the log format, helps students choose readers, and checks the log twice during the term.
Keep a log with a five-sentence summary and an opinion with reasons for each of three books or stories.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Log is complete and regularly kept

blocks.heading: SBA plan 8: Class wall newspaper
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Competency 7: Uses English creatively and innovatively in written communication
7.5 Writes simple compositions on different types of topics (Grades 8 and 9)
Newspaper writing: news report, notice, story or poem, puzzle
Students will be able to write in different formats and work together to publish them.
Forms groups, shows sample wall newspapers, sets deadlines, and monitors each member's contribution.
Plan, write, edit and display a wall newspaper with at least four items; each member writes one item.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Teamwork: each member's part is shown

blocks.heading: SBA plan 9: Formal letter under timed conditions
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Competency 7: Uses English creatively and innovatively in written communication
Letter of complaint or request on a local issue
Students will be able to write a formal letter of about 150 words with the correct format and tone.
Sets the task with clear points to include, and supervises the timed writing.
Write a formal letter covering all the given points in 30 minutes.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Correct format (addresses, date, salutation, subject, close)
Accurate grammar and a suitable formal tone

blocks.heading: SBA plan 10: Two-minute speech
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Competency 8: Communicates clearly, fluently and concisely
A topic from the textbook (for example healthy food or careers)
Students will be able to deliver an organised two-minute speech.
Gives topics a week ahead, shows how to open and close a speech, and marks each speech.
Prepare and deliver a two-minute speech with an opening, main points and a closing.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Clear main idea with supporting points

blocks.heading: SBA plan 11: Survey and report
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Competency 5: Extracts necessary information from various types of texts
5.3 Transfers information into other forms (Grades 10 and 11)
Students will be able to present survey results in a bar chart and a short report.
Explains how to conduct a survey and describe a chart, and gives useful phrases.
Conduct a class survey, draw a bar chart and write a short report on the findings.

blocks.heading: SBA plan 12: Group presentation
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Presents information clearly to an audience.
Delivers a structured presentation with signposting. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
A textbook topic (for example the cyber world or continuing education)
Students will be able to deliver a structured group presentation on a textbook topic.
Forms groups, assigns topics, teaches signposting language, and assesses the presentations.
Research, plan and deliver a five-minute presentation in which every member speaks.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Clear delivery and every member takes part

blocks.heading: SBA plan 13: Formal email
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Writes formal emails for a specific purpose.
Writes a clear formal email with the correct structure and tone. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
Email to the principal of another school about a joint event
Students will be able to write a formal email that covers all the required points.
Sets the task with the required points and supervises the writing.

blocks.heading: SBA plan 14: Discursive essay
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Writes an essay that discusses both sides of an issue.
Organises a balanced argument with examples. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
An issue from the textbook units
Students will be able to write a balanced essay of about 250 words.
Gives two or three questions, revises essay structure, and supervises the writing.
Choose one question and write an essay of about 250 words.

blocks.heading: SBA plan 15: Job application and interview
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
One period for the letter, 5 minutes per interview
Writes a covering letter and answers interview questions appropriately. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
Job advertisements and covering letters (Unit 8, Employment)
Students will be able to apply for a job in writing and answer interview questions politely and clearly.
Provides advertisements, revises the covering-letter format, and conducts short interviews.
Write a covering letter for one advertisement and take part in a short interview for that job.

blocks.heading: English Literature (O/L)
text: One of the prescribed novels is assessed by the school as well as examined, and the school chooses which. The three novels on the list shown on our O/L Literature page are The Prince and the Pauper, Bringing Tony Home and The Vendor of Sweets; confirm the list for your examination year.

blocks.heading: SBA plan 16: Poetry (analysing theme and techniques)
rows: Responds critically to poetry by identifying themes and poetic devices.
Explores the underlying meanings, tone and imagery used by poets to convey central messages. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
Selected O/L poems (for example To the Evening Star or Richard Cory)
Students will be able to analyse poetic techniques such as metaphor, simile and personification and explain how they contribute to the poem's theme.
Introduces the poem, explains core poetic devices, provides a rubric, and guides students on how to structure a literary commentary.
Select one prescribed poem, analyse three major poetic devices used in it, write a 150-word commentary, and present their main findings to the class.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Understanding of themes and central message
Correct identification and analysis of poetic devices

blocks.heading: SBA plan 17: Short stories (character analysis)
rows: Analyses character traits, motives and relationships within a short story.
Demonstrates empathy and critical understanding of characters by interpreting their actions and dialogue. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
Prescribed short stories (for example The Lumber Room or The Fly)
Group role play and character sketch presentation
Students will be able to extract textual evidence to justify a character's behaviour and mindset.
Divides the class into small groups, assigns specific characters from a short story, and monitors the brainstorming sessions.
Collaborate to create a visual character profile poster and perform a short three-minute role play depicting a crucial scene from that character's perspective.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Accurate depiction of character traits based on the text

blocks.heading: SBA plan 18: Novel: The Vendor of Sweets (theme exploration)
rows: Evaluates major themes and cultural conflicts in an extended text.
Examines the generation gap, the clash of East and West, and illusion versus reality in Malgudi. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
Novel: The Vendor of Sweets by R. K. Narayan
Students will write a coherent essay analysing how the conflict between Jagan and Mali represents the clash between traditional Indian values and Western modernisation.
Formulates analytical essay prompts, sets clear guidelines for thesis statements, and ensures students have access to their unmarked novels during the session.
Choose one prompt, formulate a thesis statement, select appropriate quotations from The Vendor of Sweets, and write a structured essay with an introduction, body paragraphs and a conclusion.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Effective use of textual quotations and references

blocks.heading: SBA plan 19: Drama (dramatised reading and stagecraft)
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Interprets drama through performance and an understanding of dramatic techniques.
Conveys character, mood and conflict through voice, movement and staging choices. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
Prescribed drama (The Bear or Twilight of a Crane)
Group dramatised reading with individual director's notes
Students will be able to perform a key scene and explain how stage directions, dialogue and action reveal character and conflict.
Selects key scenes, explains dramatic techniques (stage directions, dramatic irony, climax), forms groups and monitors rehearsals.
Rehearse and perform a key scene of about four minutes, and each write a short set of director's notes (about 100 words) explaining their staging choices.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Director's notes explain staging choices with reference to the text

blocks.heading: SBA plan 20: Novel (reading journal)
rows: 1st / 2nd / 3rd (as set in your school's SBA plan)
Over one term, with journal checks every two weeks
Responds personally and critically to an extended text.
Tracks plot, character development and themes across a novel. *(Sample wording: use the competency level in your Teacher's Guide.)*
The novel your school has selected for SBA
Students will be able to record and reflect on plot, characters and themes as they read, supported by quotations.
Explains the journal format (chapter summary, character notes, key quotation, personal response), sets the reading schedule and checks journals regularly.
Keep a journal entry for each chapter or section with a short summary, notes on one character, one key quotation with a comment, and a personal response.

blocks.heading: Criteria for marking
rows: Insight into character development and themes
Regular, complete and neatly kept journal

blocks.heading: 1. English Only Day
rows: The Principal, through the relevant sectional head
Many pupils understand English but rarely use it outside the English period. One day a week or a month when English is spoken throughout the school gives them a real reason to use it.
To give pupils regular practice in everyday spoken English; to build confidence; to involve all staff in supporting English.
All pupils from the selected grades, with teachers and non-academic staff.
To be decided with the school administration and entered in the school calendar.
To be decided (for example, the school hall or classrooms).
A short English assembly; English announcements; a list of useful phrases displayed in each classroom; English greetings at the gate; a small reward for classes that use English well.
Teacher in charge; English teachers to prepare phrase lists; prefects to encourage English use; class teachers to record participation.
Phrase charts, a notice board, simple certificates or badges.
List each item with quantity and a local price you have checked. Leave out anything the school already has.
For example, school development funds, class funds or sponsorship. Confirm with the principal.
Class participation records; a short pupil questionnaire after each month.
Pupils use more spoken English and feel less afraid of making mistakes.
Signatures and dates: teacher in charge, sectional head, principal.

blocks.heading: 2. English Day
rows: The Principal, through the relevant sectional head
An annual English Day lets pupils show their English skills to parents and the school community.
To give pupils a stage for English; to discover talent; to raise interest in English.
Pupils of all grades, parents and staff.
To be decided with the school administration and entered in the school calendar.
To be decided (for example, the school hall or classrooms).
Inter-house or inter-class competitions (recitation, speech, singing, drama, spelling); a final programme with the winners; an exhibition of pupils' written work.
Organising committee; competition judges; stage and sound; hospitality; publicity.
Hall, sound system, certificates, trophies or prizes, decorations.
List each item with quantity and a local price you have checked. Leave out anything the school already has.
For example, school development funds, class funds or sponsorship. Confirm with the principal.
Participation numbers, feedback from parents and staff, a short report with photographs.
Greater interest in English and a list of talented pupils for zonal competitions.
Signatures and dates: teacher in charge, sectional head, principal.

blocks.heading: 3. Class Reading Programme
rows: The Principal, through the relevant sectional head
Many pupils read very little in English. A short daily or weekly reading time with a class reading corner builds the reading habit.
To build the reading habit; to improve vocabulary and comprehension.
To be decided with the school administration and entered in the school calendar.
To be decided (for example, the school hall or classrooms).
A class reading corner with graded books; a regular reading time; a simple reading log; a monthly best-reader recognition.
Teacher in charge; class teachers; librarian; pupil reading monitors.
Graded readers, a shelf or box, reading logs.
List each item with quantity and a local price you have checked. Leave out anything the school already has.
For example, school development funds, class funds or sponsorship. Confirm with the principal.
Reading logs; a short reading test at the start and end of the term.
Pupils read more and show better comprehension.
Signatures and dates: teacher in charge, sectional head, principal.

blocks.heading: 4. English Wall Newspaper
rows: The Principal, through the relevant sectional head
A wall newspaper gives pupils a real audience for their writing.
To encourage writing; to develop teamwork; to display pupils' work.
